architectureFigure.caption: Overview of the unified supervision framework for large-scale e-commerce retrieval. The system integrates human and relevance cross encoder labeled relevance scores, item ranks from existing retrieval channels, and user engagement signals to generate a context-rich supervision target to train bi-encoder model.

authors: Shasvat Desai, Md Omar Faruk Rokon, Jhalak Nilesh Acharya, Isha Shah, Hong Yao, Utkarsh Porwal, Kuang-chih Lee

breakthroughAssessment.justification: This paper presents a strong contribution to the field of e-commerce search, particularly for sponsored content retrieval. Its novelty lies in unifying graded semantic relevance, multi-channel retrieval prior, and user engagement into a single, robust supervision framework for bi-encoder training, with semantic relevance as the primary signal. This addresses known issues of sparsity and noisiness in engagement-only supervision. The rigorous evaluation, including both offline and online A/B tests at a large e-commerce platform (Walmart), demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over the existing production system across key business metrics. While not a paradigm shift, it provides a highly useful and effective method for improving industrial retrieval systems.

coreProblem.concreteExample: In Walmart’s e-commerce sponsored search, user engagement on ad items is often structurally sparse because ad impressions are limited by factors beyond relevance, such as auction outcomes, bid competitiveness, and advertiser budgets. This leads to weak query-item relevance despite potential user interactions.
coreProblem.statement: Modern search systems rely on user engagement signals (e.g., clicks) to supervise bi-encoder retrieval training at scale. However, engagement is an imperfect and noisy proxy for semantic relevance, often influenced by non-relevance factors like popularity, promotion, or price. Additionally, engagement data can be sparse, especially in contexts like sponsored search where ad slot availability and budgets limit impressions, hindering effective learning.
whyItMatters: Engagement-derived labels introduce systematic noise, biasing retrievers toward highly engaged but weakly relevant items.
Sparsity of engagement data for many candidates (especially cold-start and long-tail items) limits learnability from engagement alone.
In sponsored search, limited ad impressions due to auctions and budgets further reduce engagement coverage, making engagement-driven learning particularly insufficient.

evaluationHighlights: Achieved +7.8% gain in Average relevance@25, +10.5% in P@25, and +5.7% in NDCG@25 compared to the production system in offline evaluation.

Demonstrated statistically significant positive lifts across various online A/B test metrics, including Sponsored Ad Impressions (+0.60%), Add to Cart Rate (+0.99%), and Total Search Page Views per Session (+0.63%).

The engagement supervision component increases the share of highly engaged items in the Top 25 retrieved set (e.g., +14.3 pp at 50th percentile, +7.0 pp at 90th percentile) without sacrificing overall relevance.

benchmarks: A proprietary evaluation set of 30,303 queries from Walmart’s sponsored search (covering high-traffic, high-revenue, long-tail, and historically under-performing queries)
metrics: Add to Cart Rate (A/B Test Lift)
Total Search Page Views per Session (A/B Test Lift)
Total Cart Page Views per Session (A/B Test Lift)
evaluationSetup.setting: Walmart’s e-commerce sponsored search retrieval, evaluating top-25 candidates (K=25) which is the optimal number of ad items for the application.

mainTakeaways: The proposed unified supervision framework significantly outperforms the production control system in offline retrieval quality metrics.

Adding the engagement signal *after* establishing relevance provides modest but consistent additional gains, helping to prioritize stronger candidates among already relevant items without degrading overall relevance.
Online A/B tests demonstrate statistically significant positive lifts across several business and ad engagement metrics, confirming real-world impact.
The model ensures that retrieved items are not only semantically relevant but also popular/highly engaged, better aligning with user preferences and downstream ranking objectives.

explanation: The framework generates a context-rich training target by combining: (i) graded relevance labels from cross-encoder teacher models and human annotations, (ii) a multi-channel retrieval prior score derived from rank positions and cross-channel agreement of production retrieval systems, and (iii) user engagement applied only to semantically relevant items to refine preferences.
This approach makes semantic relevance the primary training signal, robustly addressing the limitations of sparse and exposure-biased engagement in sponsored search.

It is presented as the first sponsored-search retrieval framework to integrate these three distinct signals (graded relevance, retrieval prior, and engagement) into a single bi-encoder training objective.
keyNovelty.main: A unified supervision framework for bi-encoder retrieval in e-commerce sponsored search, prioritizing semantic relevance as the primary training signal, while incorporating multi-channel retrieval priors for hard negative mining and user engagement as a preference signal only among relevant items.

keyTerms.definition: A type of neural network architecture where two inputs (e.g., query and item) are independently encoded into separate dense embedding vectors, and their similarity is computed in the embedding space. This allows for low-latency retrieval as item embeddings can be pre-computed.

A type of neural network that takes a pair of inputs (e.g., query and item) and processes them together to compute a relevance score. They are typically more accurate but slower than bi-encoders for large-scale retrieval.

A technique used in training deep learning models, particularly in retrieval and ranking, to identify and prioritize negative examples that are difficult for the model to distinguish from positive examples, thereby improving model discrimination.
A pair consisting of a user query and a retrieved item, used as a fundamental unit in information retrieval and search systems.

prerequisites: User engagement signals (clicks, orders, add-to-cart, views)
Contrastive learning and Cosine Similarity Loss

comparisonToPriorWork: Prior deployed search systems typically rely on noisy and sparse user engagement signals for supervision, which biases retrievers toward highly engaged but weakly relevant items; this work makes semantic relevance the primary signal.

Previous methods incorporating explicit relevance signals usually use them as secondary constraints (e.g., filtering engagement-derived positives), with engagement remaining the primary supervision source, whereas this work reverses that priority.

This work integrates graded relevance, multi-channel retrieval prior, and user engagement into a *single, unified* supervision framework for bi-encoder training, which is novel for sponsored search retrieval, unlike prior works that used these signals separately or with a single dominant signal.

The approach directly addresses the limitations of sparse and exposure-biased engagement in sponsored search (due to ad-slot auctions, bids, and budgets) by making relevance the foundational training signal.
limitations: The paper does not explicitly list limitations in a dedicated section; however, it frames the issues of engagement noisiness, sparsity, and exposure bias in prior methods as problems that its unified supervision framework is designed to overcome.

modeling.label: Raw Engagement Score
modeling.value: $E_{raw}(q, i) = \log(1 + \lambda_1 O(q, i) + \lambda_2 A(q, i) + \lambda_3 C(q, i) + \lambda_4 V(q, i))$

modeling.label: Normalized and Smoothed Engagement Score
modeling.value: $E(q, i) = E_{raw}(q, i) / (\max_{i' \in C(q)} E_{raw}(q, i') + \epsilon)$ and $\tilde{E}(q, i) = \sigma(k (E(q, i) - 0.5))$ where $\sigma(x) = 1 / (1 + e^{-x})$ and $k=8$.

modeling.label: Unified Relevance-Rank Score (for positive QIPs)
modeling.value: $y_{rel-rank}(q, i) = \alpha \cdot rel\_score(q, i) + \beta \cdot \pi(q, i) + \gamma \cdot C(q, i)$ with $\alpha=0.6, \beta=0.3, \gamma=0.1$.

modeling.label: Irrelevant QIP Difficulty Score (for negative QIPs)

pipelineFlow: Gather query-item interaction data, production retrieval ranks, and human annotations.
Generate graded relevance labels for QIPs using a cascade of cross-encoder teacher models and human annotations.
Compute multi-channel retrieval prior scores and channel agreement scores based on item ranks from existing production retrieval systems.
Process historical user engagement signals to derive normalized and smoothed engagement scores.
Combine the graded relevance, retrieval prior, and engagement signals into a unified supervision target score for each QIP, differentiating between positive and negative QIPs.

Fine-tune a MiniLM bi-encoder model using the unified supervision scores with Cosine Similarity Loss and Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking (cachedMNR) Loss, employing curriculum-based weighting sampling.
Deploy the trained bi-encoder model for sponsored search retrieval to outperform the current production system in offline and online evaluations.

problemDefinition.label: Query-Item Pair (QIP)
problemDefinition.value: A pair $(q, i)$ consisting of a query $q$ and an item $i$.

problemDefinition.label: Relevance Rating
problemDefinition.value: An ordinal 5-point relevance rating $Rel(q, i) \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$, where 0 is 'Embarrassing' and 4 is 'Excellent', indicating the degree of intent fulfillment.

technicalDetails.reproducibility: The paper provides details on the evaluation setup, including a test set of 30,303 queries, the use of a MiniLM bi-encoder, specific loss functions (Cosine Similarity Loss, cachedMNR), and hyperparameter tuning for weighting signals (lambda, alpha, beta, gamma, mu_rel, lambda_eng) on a validation set. The evaluation also uses a hybrid judging setup combining human and model-based annotations for 5-point relevance labels. These details contribute to reproducibility.

systemModules.details: Produces a 5-point ordinal relevance rating for QIPs using a cascade of cross-encoder teacher models (Gemma-1B, Gemma-2B, LLaMA-3 8B) and human annotations. These ratings are normalized to a score $rel\_score(q, i) \in [0, 1]$.
systemModules.name: Graded Relevance Label Generator
systemModules.role: Provides the primary fine-grained semantic supervision for nuanced understanding.

systemModules.details: Derived from item rank positions and consensus across multiple existing production retrieval channels. It assigns a monotonic prior score $\pi(q, i)$ and a multi-channel agreement score $C(q, i)$.
systemModules.name: Multi-channel Retrieval Prior Score Generator
systemModules.role: Encapsulates production system strengths and failure modes, facilitating hard-negative mining by identifying highly-ranked but irrelevant candidates and reinforcing highly-ranked and relevant positives.

systemModules.details: Aggregates behavioral counts (orders, add-to-cart, clicks, views) into a log-compressed signal $E_{raw}(q, i)$, then normalized within query and sigmoid-smoothed to $\tilde{E}(q, i) \in [0, 1]$.
systemModules.name: Historical User Engagement Processor
systemModules.role: Refines supervision for semantically relevant QIPs as a preference signal, aligning results with user preferences (e.g., items with promotions, low prices, good reviews).

systemModules.details: Combines the three signals. For positive QIPs ($Rel(q, i) \in \{3, 4\}$), it computes a unified relevance-rank score $y_{rel-rank}(q, i)$ from semantic label, rank-prior, and channel consensus, then adds an engagement boost $\tilde{E}(q, i)$ to form $y_{rel-rank-eng}(q, i)$. For negative QIPs ($Rel(q, i) \in \{0, 1, 2\}$), it computes an irrelevant QIP difficulty score $y_{irrel-rank-lex}(q, i)$ from rank-prior and token similarity.
systemModules.name: Unified Supervision Target Generator
systemModules.role: Synthesizes the three heterogeneous sources into a single context-rich training target for the bi-encoder model.

systemModules.details: A MiniLM bi-encoder fine-tuned using the unified supervision scores via Cosine Similarity Loss and Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking (cachedMNR) Loss. Irrelevant QIP difficulty scores are used in curriculum-based weighting sampling.
systemModules.name: Bi-encoder Retrieval Model (MiniLM)
systemModules.role: The core retrieval model trained to output embeddings for queries and items, enabling efficient semantic search.

thesis: We propose a unified supervision framework for bi-encoder retrieval in Walmart's sponsored search that makes semantic relevance the primary training signal, while incorporating multi-channel retrieval prior and user engagement as a preference signal among relevant items, ultimately outperforming the current production system in both offline evaluation and online A/B tests with consistent gains.
title: Unified Supervision for Walmart’s Sponsored Search Retrieval via Joint Semantic Relevance and Behavioral Engagement Modeling
